characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
327 women

Inclusion criteria: normal-risk nulliparous women aged 18 to under 40 years with singleton pregnancies and no contraindications to labour induction. Participants must agree to outpatient induction at 39 weeks and have no relevant medical issues assessed by a doctor on a case-by-case basis, inclusive of systems disorders outlined in the exclusion criteria. They must live within 30 minutes or 15 km of the hospital and have transport available at all times during the induction period. Additionally, a normal amniotic fluid index (AFI) between 8 cm and 20 cm and a Biophysical Profile Score (BPS) of 8/8 at 39 weeks gestation is required. Furthermore, participants must have a Bishop's score of less than 6 at Visit 2.

Exclusion criteria: multiparous women with a uterine scar, low-lying placenta, BMI exceeding 35kg/m2, multiple gestation, known fetal anomalies, fetal growth restriction, or oligohydramnios, and maternal health problems such as hypertensive, cardiac, renal, diabetes, pulmonary, or hepatic diseases directly affecting the woman's risk status. Additionally, exclusion criteria include lack of transport to the hospital, living more than 30 minutes or 15 km away, difficulty understanding the protocol and follow-up instructions, and gestational age less than 39+0 or greater than 39+4 weeks at the time of induction. Other contraindications involve factors such as ongoing labour, previous uterine surgery, clinical suspicion of cephalopelvic disproportion, fetal malpresentation, non-reassuring fetal testing, history of major surgery or cervical rupture, pelvic inflammatory disease, hypersensitivity to dinoprostone, placenta previa, unexplained vaginal bleeding, or evidence of infection.

characteristics.value: Labour induction in an outpatient setting - a multicenter randomized controlled trial. OPTION - OutPatienT InductiON

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
17,782 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 to 45 years, capable of communicating with the hospital, and experiencing uncomplicated live singleton pregnancies at gestational ages between 37+0 to 41+6 weeks according to crown-rump length or biparietal diameter (<55 mm) on first or second-trimester ultrasound. Additionally, participants must have an engaged and stable cephalic presentation. Clinical examination before induction, including Leopold's maneuvers, digital cervical exam, abdominal ultrasound, temperature, blood pressure, and cardiotocography scan, must reveal an engaged and stable cephalic presentation with a Bishop score of less than 6 (less than 5 in parous women) and a cardiotocography classified as normal according to the antepartal Swedish Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology criteria. Furthermore, during the first 45 minutes after induction, in cases of induction with the balloon method, cardiotocography must be classified as normal according to the same criteria.

Exclusion criteria: a history of previous uterine surgery with uterine scar (e.g. caesarean section or myomectomy), pregestational or medically treated gestational diabetes (insulin or metformin), dietary treated gestational diabetes with large for gestational age fetus, preeclampsia or unstable hypertensive disease, multiple pregnancies, intrauterine fetal death (IUFD) in current or previous pregnancies, known fetal malformations or conditions affecting newborn care, congenital uterine malformations, conditions requiring inpatient care, and inability to reach the hospital within a reasonable time. Clinical examination before induction must exclude small for gestational age (small for gestational age (SGA), intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), or fetal growth restriction (FGA), oligohydramnios, polyhydramnios, maternal pyrexia, known low-lying placenta, and high head. Additionally, exclusion criteria include premature rupture of membranes (PROM) exceeding 30 hours or known colonization with group B streptococci. Observations within the first 45 minutes after induction must also consider adverse events such as heavy bleeding, pain, and premature rupture of membranes, if not the indication for induction, as well as the start of contractions.
